claims.text: Coupling atomistic molecular-dynamics simulations with a machine-learning surrogate trained on local atomic descriptors can predict fusion and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across high-entropy alloys.

The proposed MD-plus-ML approach can predict melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, volume change at melting, and key liquid-phase thermodynamic properties with errors on the order of 5% relative to experiment.
CrMnFeCoNi, NbMoTaW, and similar alloys provide representative coverage of different HEA compositional families.
NPT molecular-dynamics temperature ramps from the solid state through melting to the fully liquid state can supply the data needed to determine fusion-related properties.
Local atomic arrangement descriptors and order parameters can be extracted from the MD trajectories.
Training machine-learning models on MD outputs from multiple compositions will enable rapid prediction over a vast HEA composition space.
Extensive MD training data covering a range of compositions will ensure predictive reliability.
Local bond-order parameters and coordination numbers are critical mediators between atomistic melting processes and macroscopic fusion properties.
High-fidelity MD simulations capture atomic-scale melting mechanisms, including coordination changes and order-disorder transitions.
A machine-learning surrogate can use local-environment descriptors to generalize fusion-property predictions across HEA compositions.
The machine-learning surrogate will accelerate evaluation across HEA composition space relative to direct atomistic simulation.
The proposed method will significantly reduce computational screening time compared with brute-force MD.
Calorimetry and complementary diffraction measurements on selected HEAs can provide experimental benchmarks for the calculated fusion properties.
The quality of empirical MD interatomic potentials limits the applicability and accuracy of the approach.
Training-set representativeness may limit applicability to exceptionally high-melting compositions or alloys with unconventional atomic arrangements.
Sparse composition-space sampling and limited transferability of local descriptors across diverse HEA systems can introduce prediction uncertainty.
Liquid-phase density can serve as an indicator of volume change at melting.
Consistent experimental deviations greater than 5-7% across multiple compositions would rule out the viability of the proposed MD-plus-ML approach.
